RbEwGnyLL58.title: CataractCoach.com with a routine cataract surgery case using phaco chop

dAzb-wU7mgU.title: YouTube dAzb-wU7mgU

lzixjGNVrWw.title: YouTube lzixjGNVrWw
lzixjGNVrWw.t1_explanation: The sequence demonstrates an uneventful small-pupil dense cataract surgery managed with a pupillary expansion device (Malyugin ring), successful capsulorhexis, prechopping, and phacoemulsification without any tears, zonular loss, or posterior capsule compromise.
lzixjGNVrWw.t2_explanation: The surgical steps progress routinely with stable anterior chamber depth, intact capsular bag, centered pupillary expansion ring, and controlled nuclear division with no intraoperative adverse events.
lzixjGNVrWw.t3_explanation: Maintaining capsular bag expansion with an ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD) and carefully guiding/dialing the trailing haptic clockwise allows the foldable acrylic IOL to safely unfold completely inside the capsular bag without traumatizing the posterior capsule or zonules.

vT4otn4YXdE.title: HumanOptics Iris Prosthesis and Sutured Capsular Tension Segment for Traumatic Cataract
vT4otn4YXdE.t1_explanation: Severe zonular dialysis/dehiscence is present, manifested by lens decentration and loss of equatorial capsular support requiring capsule retractors, an Ahmed capsular tension segment (CTS) with scleral suture fixation, and subsequent artificial iris implantation.
vT4otn4YXdE.t2_explanation: Extensive zonular dialysis is demonstrated by the displacement of the capsular bag, the use of multiple flexible capsular retractors to stabilize the capsular equator during lens removal, and transscleral suture fixation of a capsular tension segment.
vT4otn4YXdE.t3_explanation: A subluxated or profoundly decentered capsular bag-IOL complex requires scleral fixation (or repositioning using scleral sutures or Yamane/flanged techniques) typically alongside anterior vitrectomy to clear prolapsed vitreous and re-establish a stable, centered optical axis.

wblfkJHRi4Q.title: YouTube wblfkJHRi4Q
wblfkJHRi4Q.t1_explanation: The surgical sequence demonstrates an uncomplicated, educational cataract procedure highlighting a tri-planar clear corneal incision, an intact continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis, and successful in-the-bag intraocular lens placement.
wblfkJHRi4Q.t2_explanation: The posterior capsule remains intact, the anterior capsulotomy is continuous and smooth, and the IOL is stable and well-centered in the capsular bag with no adverse events.
wblfkJHRi4Q.t3_explanation: In standard cataract surgery, a continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis is created by initiating a tear via anterior capsule puncture (with a cystotome or forceps tip) and grasping and shearing the capsular flap circumferentially using capsulorhexis (Utrata) forceps.

xt6AKGzD2Co.title: YouTube xt6AKGzD2Co
xt6AKGzD2Co.t1_explanation: The surgical sequence demonstrates an uneventful and routine phacoemulsification procedure, progressing smoothly through incision, capsulorhexis, nuclear disassembly, cortical removal, and intraocular lens implantation without any capsular tear, vitreous loss, or other surgical complication.
xt6AKGzD2Co.t2_explanation: All phases of the surgery, from clear corneal incision and capsulorhexis through phacoemulsification and IOL placement, proceed without capsular rupture, zonular dehiscence, iris trauma, or any adverse event.
xt6AKGzD2Co.t3_explanation: Following intraocular lens insertion and removal of ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD), the standard final steps of an uncomplicated clear-corneal cataract surgery involve thorough evacuation of viscoelastic from the anterior segment and stromal hydration of the corneal paracentesis and main wound to ensure a watertight seal and restore physiological intraocular pressure.

0xUbMicNy-w.title: CataractCoach™ 2657: CataractQuiz™: Why did this happen? Help with this mystery case!
0xUbMicNy-w.t1_explanation: The intraoperative cataract extraction and intraocular lens implantation were completed uneventfully without surgical adverse events such as capsule rupture or zonulopathy.
0xUbMicNy-w.t2_explanation: The procedure demonstrates an intact capsulorhexis, complete phacoemulsification, and successful in-the-bag IOL implantation without any intraoperative complications, classifying it as Routine / Normal.
0xUbMicNy-w.t3_explanation: In crowded anterior segments and shallow chambers, generous use of a dispersive ophthalmic viscosurgical device protects the fragile corneal endothelium from ultrasound energy and fluid turbulence, while low-flow fluidics minimizes turbulence.

2PnbLBFKiyQ.title: Argentinian Flag sign 6-19-2016.  Surgery and Narration by Shannon Wong, MD
2PnbLBFKiyQ.t1_explanation: An intraoperative Argentinian flag sign (spontaneous bilateral radial extension of the anterior capsulotomy tear) occurred upon initial capsule puncture in an intumescent white cataract.
2PnbLBFKiyQ.t2_explanation: Frames 5 to 7 clearly demonstrate the classic Argentinian flag sign, where high intralenticular pressure causes the trypan blue-stained anterior capsule to rapidly tear radially toward the equator on opposite sides, exposing the underlying white lens cortex.
2PnbLBFKiyQ.t3_explanation: The first critical step upon encountering a runaway radial tear or Argentinian flag sign is to immediately decompress and flatten the convex anterior lens surface by injecting a high-viscosity ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD) into the anterior chamber, which eliminates vector forces driving the tear toward the equator before converting or rescuing the capsulotomy.

9E_jRdOnuqw.title: Crazy Dislocated Traumatic Cataract with Sutured Capsular Tension Segments
9E_jRdOnuqw.t1_explanation: Extensive zonular dialysis/dehiscence is present, requiring the intraoperative placement of multiple capsular retractors to stabilize the capsular bag during lens removal, followed by scleral suture fixation of a capsular stabilization device.
9E_jRdOnuqw.t2_explanation: The surgical sequence demonstrates management of profound zonular dialysis/dehiscence, highlighted by the deployment of capsular tension hooks engaging the capsulorhexis edge, followed by implantation and transscleral suture fixation (Gore-Tex/Prolene) of a capsular tension segment/device.
9E_jRdOnuqw.t3_explanation: A standard CTR alone redistributes forces but cannot recenter or anchor a bag with focal defects exceeding 3–4 clock hours (>120 degrees); a sutured Capsular Tension Segment (CTS) or Cionni modified CTR anchored to the scleral wall provides necessary focal support and recentration.

QJwvHv9pBxU.t2_explanation: Visual inspection reveals severe zonular laxity/dehiscence (phacodonesis) with marked capsulorhexis decentration and anterior capsular striae, requiring capsular retractors to support the bag complex during cataract extraction.
QJwvHv9pBxU.t3_explanation: In eyes with localized zonular dehiscence or significant zonular weakness, inserting capsular retractors (Mackool hooks) to support the capsulorhexis edge and/or a capsular tension ring (CTR) redistributes forces and stabilizes the capsular bag before nucleus emulsification.

zaL9vzyCJSI.title: Phaco Incision OCT & Live Video Analysis in Cataract Surgery
zaL9vzyCJSI.t1_explanation: The video frames depict incision construction and intraoperative OCT analysis of the clear corneal/limbal incision. There is no intraoperative complication or structural damage.

zaL9vzyCJSI.t3_explanation: Minor superficial bleeding from conjunctival or episcleral vessels at the limbus is safely managed with gentle external irrigation using balanced salt solution (BSS) or a cotton-tipped applicator, as it does not involve or threaten intraocular structures.

-iy_f_6SD9Y.title: CataractCoach™ 2751: cleaning the bag and then it splits open
-iy_f_6SD9Y.t1_explanation: A posterior capsule rupture (PCR) occurs during posterior capsule polishing/cleaning, characterized by a visible linear split in the capsule.
-iy_f_6SD9Y.t2_explanation: Inspection of early frames shows the posterior capsule splitting during aspiration/polishing, followed by OVD injection to stabilize the anterior chamber and subsequent placement of a three-piece IOL with optic capture.
-iy_f_6SD9Y.t3_explanation: Abrupt withdrawal of the instrument drops anterior chamber pressure, causing vitreous to prolapse forward and extending the tear; dispersive viscoelastic must be injected via a paracentesis prior to instrument removal to maintain pressure and tamponade the vitreous face.

2Q4cSQBrGiQ.title: CataractCoach™ 2770: first ever posterior capsule rupture
2Q4cSQBrGiQ.t1_explanation: A tear in the posterior capsule occurred during lens removal, leading to a posterior capsule rupture requiring management with vitrectomy/viscoat stabilization.
2Q4cSQBrGiQ.t2_explanation: Direct visualization reveals a breach of the posterior capsule during phacoemulsification, with subsequent introduction of a vitrectomy cutter and infusion line to manage the defect.
2Q4cSQBrGiQ.t3_explanation: Dry aspiration (e.g., using a cannula or syringe) or a bimanual vitrectomy cutter with a high cut rate and low vacuum allows controlled stripping and removal of cortex without exerting traction on the vitreous base or enlarging the capsular tear.

4_tQy09RJD4.title: Managing complex cataract surgery: Advanced strategies (Malyugin)
4_tQy09RJD4.t1_explanation: The submitted frames are from an academic presentation regarding cataract surgery history, lens design, and complicated scenarios rather than a surgical complication video; no intraoperative surgical adverse event is observed.
4_tQy09RJD4.t2_explanation: The imagery consists of an educational slide deck and standard clinical reference images with no active intraoperative complication, corresponding to Routine / Normal.
4_tQy09RJD4.t3_explanation: In cases of severe pupillary miosis, small pupils, or intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS), mechanical pupil expansion devices such as the Malyugin ring or iris retractor hooks are standardly utilized to achieve stable, wide pupillary dilation and prevent iris trauma.

5P41f5qxgNE.title: CataractCoach™ 2975: traumatic cataract with zonular loss
5P41f5qxgNE.t1_explanation: The video demonstrates a traumatic cataract case with extensive zonular dialysis and loss, requiring surgical placement of trocars for posterior support and a capsular tension device.
5P41f5qxgNE.t2_explanation: Frame 1 highlights a large area of zonular dehiscence (red dashed line and arrow). The surgeon uses vitrectomy trocars and prepares a capsular tension ring (CTR) to manage the zonular dialysis.
5P41f5qxgNE.t3_explanation: Zonular loss exceeding 3-4 clock hours (especially up to 6 clock hours) cannot be supported by an unsutured standard CTR alone; it necessitates capsular retractors for intraoperative stabilization and a sutured capsular tension segment (CTS) or modified CTR to provide permanent scleral fixation and center the bag.

5iIdOj5yJNM.title: CataractCoach™ 2983: lot of phacodonesis in pseudo-exfoliation
5iIdOj5yJNM.t1_explanation: Severe zonular laxity and phacodonesis secondary to pseudoexfoliation syndrome required the intraoperative placement of flexible capsular retractors/hooks to stabilize the capsular bag during lens removal.
5iIdOj5yJNM.t2_explanation: The video demonstrates marked zonular instability/phacodonesis necessitating circumferential capsular hook placement to stabilize the lens-capsule complex during phacoemulsification.
5iIdOj5yJNM.t3_explanation: In eyes with pseudoexfoliation and progressive zonulopathy, capsular bag stabilization using a capsular tension ring (CTR) or segment, combined with optic capture or sulcus fixation of a 3-piece IOL (or scleral suture fixation), provides reliable long-term centration and stability.

6fktu4xwIdU.title: CataractCoach™ 2931: young registrar meets Argentinian flag!
6fktu4xwIdU.t1_explanation: An intraoperative complication occurred in an intumescent cataract where high intralenticular pressure resulted in a spontaneous, rapid tear of the anterior capsule extending to the periphery, known as the Argentinian Flag Sign.
6fktu4xwIdU.t2_explanation: Following the initial capsular puncture under trypan blue visualization, the anterior capsule spontaneously tore radially across the entire diameter into the zonular periphery, exposing white cortex in a characteristic Argentinian Flag configuration.
6fktu4xwIdU.t3_explanation: Injecting a cohesive or heavy ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD) flattens the dome of the intumescent lens, counteracts vitreous upthrust, and relieves zonular vector forces; micro-scissors are then utilized to make a small snip directed centrally, enabling the tear to be safely redirected into a continuous curved capsulorhexis.

6zP9-kFTW4I.title: CataractCoach™ 3017: Argentinian flag in Expert Hands
6zP9-kFTW4I.t1_explanation: An intraoperative anterior capsule radial tear occurred during capsulotomy initiation, manifesting as the classic Argentinian flag sign in an intumescent cataract.
6zP9-kFTW4I.t2_explanation: Upon puncturing the trypan blue-stained anterior capsule, high intralenticular pressure immediately caused spontaneous radial extension of the capsular tear across the lens to the periphery, creating the characteristic white-and-blue 'Argentinian flag sign'.
6zP9-kFTW4I.t3_explanation: Decompressing the intralenticular compartment by needle aspiration of liquefied milky cortex under high anterior chamber pressure provided by a heavy cohesive/viscoadaptive OVD prevents spontaneous vector propagation of the capsule edge towards the equator.

DH_iMVHi8OE.title: Ruptured posterior capsule during cataract surgery
DH_iMVHi8OE.t1_explanation: A posterior capsule rupture (PCR) occurs during the procedure, visible as a tear in the posterior capsule during cortical removal/cleanup.
DH_iMVHi8OE.t2_explanation: Inspection of the posterior capsule demonstrates a distinct breach/tear with visible capsular edges under the red reflex, confirming a posterior capsule rupture (PCR).
DH_iMVHi8OE.t3_explanation: When the posterior capsule is compromised but the anterior capsulorhexis rim remains intact and well-supported, a 3-piece IOL should be placed in the ciliary sulcus, ideally with optic capture through the rhexis to ensure centration and stability. Single-piece acrylic lenses should never be placed in the sulcus due to the risk of uveitis-glaucoma-hyphema (UGH) syndrome.

HIbazijhpzY.title: How to manage a posterior capsule rupture in cataract surgery
HIbazijhpzY.t1_explanation: A posterior capsule rupture occurs during cortical cleanup, visualized as a breach in the posterior capsule with vitreous presentation requiring anterior vitrectomy.
HIbazijhpzY.t2_explanation: Visual inspection reveals a distinct tear in the posterior capsule during irrigation/aspiration, followed by suturing of the main wound and bimanual anterior vitrectomy to clear prolapsed vitreous.
HIbazijhpzY.t3_explanation: Modern anterior vitrectomy principles dictate using a high cutting rate to minimize traction on the vitreous base and retina, low-to-moderate vacuum, and separate bimanual paracenteses to prevent wound hydration and maintain a stable anterior chamber.

KXDOVl0tLu8.title: CataractCoach™ 2807: phaco probe breaks the capsule
KXDOVl0tLu8.t1_explanation: An intraoperative posterior capsule rupture occurs when the phacoemulsification probe directly aspirates and tears the posterior capsule during removal of the final nuclear/cortical material.
KXDOVl0tLu8.t2_explanation: Direct visual inspection of the posterior capsule shows an explicit break and margin edge formation created by the phaco tip (confirmed by the on-screen annotation 'Phaco probe breaks the capsule'). Subsequent frames show viscoelastic tamponade and placement/stabilization of an intraocular lens.
KXDOVl0tLu8.t3_explanation: Withdrawing the phaco probe suddenly causes immediate anterior chamber shallowing and pressure collapse, which invites vitreous prolapse forward through the tear and can rapidly enlarge the capsular defect. The critical first step is maintaining the probe in place while simultaneously injecting dispersive OVD through a side port to maintain chamber depth and tamponade the vitreous face.

OEozdFTc9SE.title: CataractCoach OEozdFTc9SE
OEozdFTc9SE.t1_explanation: The frames demonstrate pre-existing or intraoperatively noted zonular weakness/dehiscence, evidenced by the characteristic 'solar eclipse sign' with a crescentic equatorial red reflex visible along the lens periphery.
OEozdFTc9SE.t2_explanation: The surgical sequence highlights zonulopathy with localized zonular dehiscence/dialysis, presenting with the 'solar eclipse sign' where the equatorial edge of the lens separates from the ciliary body.
OEozdFTc9SE.t3_explanation: Placement of a capsular tension ring (CTR) redistributes forces evenly to remaining intact zonules, stabilizes the capsular equator, prevents capsular collapse, and allows safe phacoemulsification and in-the-bag IOL placement.

biE_ghq1yZ0.title: CataractCoach™ 2711: tPA for supra-choroidal hemorrhage
biE_ghq1yZ0.t1_explanation: The video demonstrates a massive suprachoroidal intraocular hemorrhage requiring surgical intervention, including sclerotomy/scleral cutdowns and administration of tPA for clot drainage.
biE_ghq1yZ0.t2_explanation: The procedure shows management of an intraocular hemorrhage (specifically a suprachoroidal hemorrhage), with scleral cutdowns performed in quadrant locations to facilitate drainage of blood/hematoma following surgical complication.
biE_ghq1yZ0.t3_explanation: Acute suprachoroidal hemorrhage mandates immediate and secure closure of all incisions to restore intraocular pressure and tamponade bleeding. Definitive clot evacuation is traditionally delayed 7-14 days to allow clot liquefaction, or managed with adjuvant recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (tPA).

fR3HDVPDLNg.title: CataractCoach™ 2776: pre-existing posterior capsule rupture
fR3HDVPDLNg.t1_explanation: A posterior capsule rupture (pre-existing from a prior intravitreal injection) is present, requiring anterior vitrectomy and sulcus IOL placement with optic capture.
fR3HDVPDLNg.t2_explanation: The procedure addresses a posterior capsule rupture (PCR), demonstrated by the lack of posterior capsular integrity, anterior vitrectomy management, and placement of a 3-piece IOL with optic capture.
fR3HDVPDLNg.t3_explanation: Hydrodissection forces fluid posterior to the lens, which will expand the posterior capsule defect and hydropulsion can immediately displace the cataractous nucleus into the vitreous cavity.

jNIiVGYwh_Y.title: CataractCoach™ 2719: traumatic cataract with zonular loss - this is tough!
jNIiVGYwh_Y.t1_explanation: The patient presents with severe traumatic zonular loss/dialysis requiring vitrector-assisted capsulotomy and scleral suture fixation for capsular bag stabilization.
jNIiVGYwh_Y.t2_explanation: The video demonstrates severe zonular dialysis/loss secondary to trauma, evidenced by vitrector-assisted capsulotomy, insertion and transscleral suture fixation of capsular support elements, and subsequent intraocular lens placement.
jNIiVGYwh_Y.t3_explanation: A vitrector-assisted capsulotomy (using a high cut rate and low/moderate aspiration) cleanly cuts the anterior capsule without generating shear or centripetal traction that could worsen pre-existing zonular dehiscence.

kAtQKjDZB6Y.title: CataractCoach™ 2866: trocar placement punctures the lens
kAtQKjDZB6Y.t1_explanation: During pars plana trocar insertion, the trocar blade entered at an incorrect angle and directly punctured the lens capsule and posterior cortex.
kAtQKjDZB6Y.t2_explanation: Iatrogenic violation of the posterior/equatorial lens capsule by the pars plana vitrectomy trocar represents an intraoperative posterior capsule rupture (PCR), leading to immediate cortical hydration and loss of capsular integrity.
kAtQKjDZB6Y.t3_explanation: Direct trocar puncture into the lens violates the posterior capsule and vitreous barrier, requiring complete cataract removal, anterior/posterior vitrectomy to clear prolapsed vitreous and lens matter, and placement of a secondary sulcus or scleral-fixated intraocular lens.

n9H2MeAJEEA.title: CataractCoach™ 2415: traumatic cataract and fibrotic capsule
n9H2MeAJEEA.t1_explanation: No intraoperative surgical complications occurred. The pre-existing traumatic fibrotic capsule was successfully managed and excised using micro-scissors, followed by uneventful phacoemulsification and IOL implantation with an intact posterior capsule.
n9H2MeAJEEA.t2_explanation: The surgical sequence demonstrates uneventful management of a complex pre-existing traumatic fibrotic cataract without intraoperative adverse events such as posterior capsule rupture, radial tears, zonular dialysis, or vitreous loss, classifying it as Routine / Normal (No Intraoperative Complication).
n9H2MeAJEEA.t3_explanation: Dense fibrotic anterior capsular plaques lose their normal elasticity and shear vectors, preventing a standard continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis; intraocular micro-scissors are necessary to segment the fibrotic tissue, which can then be grasped and shaped into an adequate opening using micro-forceps.

qWeE-Va-sOM.title: CataractCoach™ 2605: combination pars plana vitrectomy and IOL exchange
qWeE-Va-sOM.t1_explanation: The surgical case demonstrates a subluxated/dislocated intraocular lens within the posterior segment requiring pars plana vitrectomy, explantation/exchange, and secondary IOL fixation.
qWeE-Va-sOM.t2_explanation: Visual inspection reveals a dislocated IOL in the vitreous cavity requiring pars plana trocars, endograspers for posterior segment mobilization, explantation, and secondary scleral-fixated IOL placement.
qWeE-Va-sOM.t3_explanation: A posteriorly dislocated IOL-capsular bag/CTR complex requires a pars plana vitrectomy to clear vitreous traction, gentle elevation and mobilization into the anterior chamber, followed by either scleral refixation or explantation and secondary IOL exchange.

uD-1a_jEdaA.title: CataractCoach™ 2139: is the posterior capsule ruptured?
uD-1a_jEdaA.t1_explanation: Although a posterior capsule rupture was intraoperatively suspected due to prominent capsular striae and folds, careful inspection under viscoelastic tamponade confirmed that the posterior capsule remained completely intact without any tear, vitreous prolapse, or surgical adverse event.
uD-1a_jEdaA.t2_explanation: The surgery is classified as Routine / Normal (H). The surgeon suspected a capsular tear, injected viscoelastic, and gently interrogated the capsule with a cannula, confirming intact capsule integrity with no rupture or zonular defect before safely completing cortex removal with coaxial I/A.
uD-1a_jEdaA.t3_explanation: Gentle visco-tamponade/visco-dissection stabilizes the anterior chamber, prevents chamber shallowing, depresses the posterior capsule, and creates a physical barrier against vitreous prolapse while allowing clear visualization and assessment of capsular integrity.

v8B-tOOqQ_4.title: CataractCoach™ 2894: How do you save the capsule now? Argentinian Flag Sign
v8B-tOOqQ_4.t1_explanation: An Argentinian flag sign occurred upon capsular puncture, characterized by rapid spontaneous extension of the anterior capsule tear bilaterally out to the periphery due to elevated intralenticular pressure in an intumescent white cataract.
v8B-tOOqQ_4.t2_explanation: Frame 3 clearly demonstrates the classic Argentinian flag sign, where the Trypan blue-stained anterior capsule splits rapidly across the visual axis, exposing a central stripe of white liquefied lens cortex flanked by blue hemiflaps.
v8B-tOOqQ_4.t3_explanation: When bilateral runaway tears occur in an intumescent cataract, the anterior capsule opening can be rescued and converted into a functional, non-extending aperture by using micro-scissors to make relaxing cuts perpendicular to the tear edges, allowing the flaps to be redirected and completed centrally.

vTKMqFLsQLc.title: CataractCoach vTKMqFLsQLc
vTKMqFLsQLc.t1_explanation: A posterior capsule rupture occurred during cortical removal, which was subsequently stabilized and converted into a continuous curvilinear posterior capsulorhexis.
vTKMqFLsQLc.t2_explanation: The frames demonstrate a defect in the posterior capsule during irrigation/aspiration that is grasped with intraocular micro-forceps to perform a posterior continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis (PCCC) prior to IOL placement.
vTKMqFLsQLc.t3_explanation: Injecting a dispersive OVD before removing instruments tamponades the anterior hyaloid face, prevents vitreous prolapse, maintains anterior chamber depth, and prevents further extension of the capsular defect.

xVaP1FEFoWU.title: CataractCoach™ 3010: traumatic zonulopathy >180 degrees
xVaP1FEFoWU.t1_explanation: Extensive traumatic zonular dialysis is evident with the lens equator visible across the pupillary aperture, requiring capsular retractors and a capsular tension device for stabilization.
xVaP1FEFoWU.t2_explanation: The frames show marked zonular dehiscence/dialysis secondary to trauma, stabilized using flexible retractors and capsular tension devices to allow safe phacoemulsification and IOL implantation.
xVaP1FEFoWU.t3_explanation: For zonular loss greater than 3 to 4 clock hours (>120°-180°), standard CTR redistribution of forces is insufficient to center the bag; a Capsular Tension Segment (CTS / Ahmed segment) or modified Cionni CTR sutured to the scleral wall using Gore-Tex or Prolene is required to provide focal transscleral vector support.
